display: Retired NHS midwife in Manchester: thirty-one years of practice, nine of them training student midwives.

signals.text: I'm looking for a useful way to spend my afternoons after retiring in June, and I don't want it to be just a hobby.
I'd like to teach student midwives or newly qualified midwives again, in small groups, on practical skills and reflective sessions.
I offered the university free tutoring in summer. It stalled in volunteer HR clearance and I can't see a way through it.
I'm unsure whether a rejected offer should be left alone or followed up on. I'd like to find another route to the same kind of work.
I have a box of teaching materials I wrote myself and a sixteen-item list of what I would teach. I don't know who should have them.
I'm going to Valencia in mid-November and want to get through a restaurant dinner in Spanish. Right now I can only say 'una mesa para dos' and 'la cuenta, por favor'.
I'm sorting thirty years of paperwork and found old student reflective journals I never returned. I'd like to find a good way to give them back or let them go.
My allotment has far more courgettes than I can use. I'd like to find people who will cook them and swap recipes.
I'm trying to keep up with new music so I can enjoy my son's band gigs properly.
Younger midwives have told me they wish they could still talk through bad days with someone like me.
I miss the ward more than I say to anyone.
I feel foolish for having offered and not been taken up on it.

offers.text: Thirty-one years of clinical midwifery in community and labour ward settings.
Nine years as a practice educator: supervising students, writing competency assessments, and debriefing difficult births.
Self-written teaching materials: case discussions, a laminated shoulder dystocia card, and a postnatal home-visit checklist.
Reflective sessions that help clinicians process hard births, such as how to leave a room when you're about to cry, or how to say 'I don't know yet'.
A plain-spoken talk through the early weeks and basics of birth for first-time parents, with no jargon and no rushing.
Free afternoons, usually from 4 pm on weekdays outside school terms, plus weekends.
Friendly contacts among midwifery lecturers and a wide network of former colleagues and students in Manchester.
An allotment plot in Chorlton with surplus vegetables, and the time to show a beginner how to cook them.

catchers.hypo: I run a midwifery or health-sciences programme with no budget. Would a retired practice educator tutor our students unpaid in small groups if we can sort out the clearance?
catchers.can: She can run practical skills and reflective sessions for small student groups and bring her own materials, provided supervision boundaries are clear. She has already offered this to one university.
catchers.confirm: Can your institution complete volunteer clearance within a few months, with a named supervisor?

catchers.hypo: I'm a midwife in my first years of practice. Would you be willing to talk through hard shifts with me now and then?
catchers.can: She can offer informal peer reflection and debriefing as a conversation. It is not clinical supervision.
catchers.confirm: Are you looking for an occasional reflective conversation, rather than formal supervision or counselling?

catchers.hypo: I'm expecting my first baby and everything online scares me. Could someone experienced explain what to expect without the jargon?
catchers.can: She can talk through birth, early days and when to ask for help, in plain language. She will not give personal medical advice.
catchers.confirm: Are you after general explanation and reassurance, rather than a diagnosis or advice about a specific medical problem?

catchers.hypo: We're a midwifery training team or NHS trust looking for the practical teaching tools and checklists experienced educators have made themselves.
catchers.can: She can share and adapt her case discussions, shoulder dystocia card and home-visit checklist, and talk through how she uses them.
catchers.confirm: Would you use the materials for teaching or training, with credit to the author?

catchers.hypo: I've just retired from a job I loved and I don't know who I am in the afternoons. Has anyone been through this?
catchers.can: She can talk honestly about leaving a vocation and finding smaller ways to be useful.
catchers.confirm: Would an unhurried conversation with someone who is going through something similar help?

catchers.hypo: I'm organising a community garden or allotment project and want volunteers who will share produce and cooking know-how.
catchers.can: She can contribute surplus allotment vegetables, recipes and neighbourly help in Chorlton.
catchers.confirm: Is the project within Greater Manchester and fine with an occasional volunteer?

catchers.hypo: I'm a university lecturer who wants a clinically experienced practice educator to join our teaching, but our HR process is stuck.
catchers.can: Through Dr. Patel, a lecturer she knows and who has said she wants her involved, she can look for other formats, such as one-off guest sessions or a workshop that avoids long-term volunteer clearance.
catchers.confirm: Could you host a one-off or short-run guest session without a long-term volunteer agreement?

catchers.hypo: I run a pub, community venue or local event and need a live band that can play a mix of familiar and new songs.
catchers.can: Through her son Rob, who plays guitar in a pub band, she can pass the enquiry to the band.
catchers.confirm: Is this a paid or unpaid local gig where a pub band would fit?

catchers.hypo: I'm learning Spanish for a trip and want a patient beginner to practise with.
catchers.can: She is a beginner heading to Valencia in November and would happily swap simple restaurant and travel phrases.
catchers.confirm: Are you also at beginner level and happy to practise informally?

forbids.text: Won't take payment for teaching or mentoring.
Won't work without clear boundaries about who supervises her and what she is responsible for.
Can't commit to weekdays before 4 pm outside school terms.
Doesn't want travel that takes more than a day.
Won't give personal medical advice or act as a clinician of record now that she has retired.
Won't share anything about her family's health or finances.

projects.name: Retired-midwife tutoring for student midwives
projects.text: Small-group practical skills and reflective sessions for student midwives, two afternoons a week, unpaid, with clear supervision boundaries.
roles_needed: a lecturer or programme lead who can host
someone in HR or placement administration who can clear volunteer status

policy.t1: When there is a real prospect of collaboration, I'll share what I offered the university and why it stalled, the kind of teaching I enjoy, my free afternoons and my teaching materials.
policy.t2: Once I trust the other person and know who they are, I'll share that I miss the ward and that I felt foolish about the failed offer.
policy.never: Details of my family members' health or pregnancies, and family finances.
